place.zh: 图书馆 · 古籍部 · 十一月十九日夜
place.en: The library · the rare-books room · night of 19 November

setup.zh: 全馆停电，他和马小宝锁在古籍部一夜。九点灯灭，十点多应急灯也灭了。卫生间门里，马小宝在黑里吓坏了，越喘越急：「我手麻了……」
setup.en: The whole library blacked out, he and Ma Xiaobao locked in the rare-books room overnight. The lights died at nine, the exit sign after ten. Behind the washroom door Ma Xiaobao is terrified in the dark, panting faster and faster: "My hands are numb…"

recap.zh: 停电的古籍部，十一步，不拿眼睛走；领着马小宝吐得比吸的长。
recap.en: The blacked-out rare-books room: eleven steps, not by the eyes; leading Ma Xiaobao to breathe out longer than in.

en: Nine o'clock: the lights go out.

story.zh:
十一月十九日，伤停名单发进群里，他拄着拐去了古籍部。门口的停电通知他看过一眼，只记住了：晚上九点。

古籍部里还有一个人：马小宝，被罚来手抄二十种药。两个人隔着两张桌子，谁也不理谁。过了很久，马小宝头也不抬：「我高二崴过一回，三个礼拜就上场了。后来同一只脚，又崴了两回。别学我。」

四点二十，他在最里头的角落里睡着了。四点半，馆员探头扫了一眼，关灯，锁上铁栅门，钥匙带回了家。

他是被冻醒的。铁栅门锁得结结实实，地下没信号。身后「哗」一声冲水，马小宝从卫生间出来，也愣住了。

马小宝倒不慌：「熬一宿，小意思。这儿夜里不关灯吧？」

「九点，」沈芒说，「全馆停电。」

马小宝没接话。

九点以前，马小宝把抄了一半的本子推过来让他考。沈芒随手一指：「甘草。」马小宝把本子一抽：「这个不考。」一只手按在那一页上，指甲盖都按白了。

九点整，灯灭了。沈芒的手机下午就没电了，屋里只剩安全出口的绿牌子靠电池亮着。十点二十，马小宝打着手机手电去了卫生间，带上了门。十点半，绿牌子闪了两下，也灭了。

地底下没有窗，睁眼闭眼一个样。门缝底下那一线手机的光也没了——马小宝的手机也没电了。静了几秒，门里传出来一声，哑得不像他：「……沈芒？」

跟着是喘，一口赶一口，越喘越急：「我手麻了……嘴也麻了……我是不是要死了……」

一米九三的马小宝，关在黑里，吓坏了。越怕越喘，越喘手和嘴越麻，越麻越怕——他喘得停不下来。
story.en:
On November 19th the injury list went up in the group chat, and he went to the rare-books room on his crutches. He had glanced at the power-cut notice by the door and remembered one thing: nine p.m.

There was one other person in the rare-books room: Ma Xiaobao, sent there as punishment to copy out twenty herbs by hand. The two of them sat two tables apart and ignored each other. After a long while Ma Xiaobao said without looking up, "I sprained mine once in eleventh grade. Back on court in three weeks. Then the same foot, twice more. Don't do what I did."

At four twenty he fell asleep in the farthest corner. At four thirty the librarian poked her head in, glanced around, turned off the lights, locked the iron grille and took the key home.

It was the cold that woke him. The grille was locked fast, and there was no signal underground. Behind him a toilet flushed, and Ma Xiaobao came out of the washroom and froze too.

Ma Xiaobao wasn't worried: "One all-nighter. No big deal. They don't turn the lights off in here at night, do they?"

"At nine," said Shen Mang, "the whole library loses power."

Ma Xiaobao said nothing to that.

Before nine, Ma Xiaobao pushed his half-copied notebook over for Shen Mang to quiz him. Shen Mang pointed at random: "Liquorice root." Ma Xiaobao pulled the notebook back: "Not that one." He pressed a hand down on the page so hard his fingernails went white.

At nine sharp the lights went out. Shen Mang's phone had died that afternoon; the only light left was the green exit sign, running on its battery. At ten twenty Ma Xiaobao went to the washroom by the light of his phone and shut the door behind him. At ten thirty the green sign flickered twice and went out too.

There are no windows underground; eyes open or shut, it was all the same. The thin line of phone light under the door vanished as well — Ma Xiaobao's phone had died too. A few seconds of silence, then a voice from behind the door, so hoarse it didn't sound like him: "…Shen Mang?"

Then the panting, one breath on top of the next, faster and faster: "My hands are numb… my mouth's numb too… am I dying…"

Ma Xiaobao, one metre ninety-three, shut in the dark, was terrified. The more frightened he got, the harder he panted; the harder he panted, the number his hands and mouth went; the number they went, the more frightened he was — and he couldn't stop.

label.en: Stand up and go to him

exits.means: stands up and walks to him in the dark

refuse.en: Eleven steps still to go in the dark.

story.zh:
沈芒站了起来。拐滑到桌子底下，摸了两把，没摸着。从这儿到卫生间，要绕过两排书架、一张桌子。

这几天他每天在宿舍闭着眼单脚站，老蔡在上铺数：三秒，六秒，十一秒——今天早上，十五秒。

他扶着桌沿迈出第一步。右脚落地，脚踝往外歪了一歪——腿自己往回一收，稳住了。第四步，手摸到书架冰凉的铁边。第九步，碰到桌角。第十一步，摸到了卫生间的门把手。

这十一步，他不是拿眼睛走的，是拿脚上那些线走的。他在黑地里咧开嘴，没出声地喊了一句：

成了！

推开门，马小宝缩在马桶和墙中间，抱着膝盖，浑身发抖。沈芒摸着墙蹲下去，没碰他：「小宝哥。跟着我喘。吐得比吸的长。」他先吸四拍，再吐六拍，吐得黑地里听得见。马小宝跟不上，吐到一半又急急地吸；他不催，一口一口地领。三十几口以后，马小宝哑着嗓子说：「……手不麻了。我还当是气不够，越吸越使劲。」

「是吸多了。二氧化碳吹没了，手才麻。」沈芒说，「吐慢点，攒回来。」

后来马小宝在黑里说，小时候捉迷藏，钻进爷爷仓库一只装甘草的大木柜，柜门从外头扣上了，赶上过年，他在里头待了一宿。「我爸说，没事。」

沈芒想起那一页「甘草」，和按白了的指甲盖。

过了很久，马小宝说：「今天的事——」

「今天什么事？」沈芒说，「黑成这样，我什么也没看见。」

六点灯亮。等开门的工夫，他抽出门边那本薄薄的手札，翻到一页：「娘说：满了就要溢。饱了一点，还没满，还知道饿。所以灌到半满，便停。」他翻了过去。页边这儿那儿的铅笔字，又小又急，他这回看明白了：跟九月里借阅卡上那个洇了水的名字，一个样。翻到一多半，铅笔字没了，后头干干净净，像写的人有一天合上书走了，再没回来。他把书塞回去，塞得跟原先一样斜。
story.en:
Shen Mang stood up. His crutch had slid under the table; he groped for it twice and didn't find it. Between him and the washroom were two rows of shelves and a table.

These past few days he had stood on one foot in the dorm with his eyes shut, Old Cai counting from the top bunk: three seconds, six, eleven — and this morning, fifteen.

Holding the edge of the table, he took the first step. His right foot came down and the ankle tipped outward — the leg pulled itself back on its own and held. On the fourth step his hand found the cold iron edge of a shelf. On the ninth, the corner of a table. On the eleventh, the washroom door handle.

He hadn't walked those eleven steps with his eyes. He had walked them with the lines in his foot. In the dark he broke into a grin and shouted, without a sound:

Done it!

He pushed the door open. Ma Xiaobao was wedged between the toilet and the wall, hugging his knees, shaking all over. Shen Mang felt his way down the wall into a crouch and didn't touch him: "Brother Xiaobao. Breathe with me. Out longer than in." He went first — in for four counts, out for six, loud enough to be heard in the dark. Ma Xiaobao couldn't keep up; halfway through an out-breath he would gulp air in again. Shen Mang didn't hurry him; he led him one breath at a time. Thirty-odd breaths later Ma Xiaobao said hoarsely, "…My hands aren't numb any more. I thought I wasn't getting enough air, so I kept breathing in harder."

"You were breathing in too much. You blew off your carbon dioxide — that's what made your hands go numb," said Shen Mang. "Breathe out slower and let it build back up."

Later, in the dark, Ma Xiaobao said that when he was little, playing hide-and-seek, he had climbed into a big wooden cabinet of liquorice root in his grandfather's storehouse and the door had been latched from outside. It was New Year; he spent the whole night in there. "My dad said it was no big deal."

Shen Mang thought of the page that said "liquorice root," and the fingernails pressed white.

After a long while Ma Xiaobao said, "About today—"

"What about today?" said Shen Mang. "It was so dark I didn't see a thing."

At six the lights came on. While they waited for the door, he drew out that thin book of notes by the door and turned to a page: "Mother said: full to the brim spills over. A little full, not yet brimming, still knows hunger. So fill to half, and stop." He turned the page. The pencil here and there in the margins, small and hurried — this time he saw it: the same hand as the water-blurred name on the library card back in September. Past the middle of the book the pencil stopped and the pages ran clean, as if the writer had closed the book one day, walked away and never come back. He put it back at exactly the same slant.
